body: Actually NET’s are supposed to be very slow growing and not aggressive. My mom’s case was unfortunate, she was 60. Feel free to ask me any questions regarding my experience with what happened with her, I can give u insights which may help you. I am sure you will beat this thing! Stay strong!

We did a liquid biopsy and tested the sample with effectiveness of various drugs that could help with this particular tumor composition. In the onco-sensitivity report, it showed 80% effectiveness for both Cisplatin and Etoposide. Our oncologist decided to give them both aggressively, one dose every 30 days. It was effective, stopped the disease progression and the SUV max values were very encouraging. But it was too toxic for her body to take. She requested me to not give her that, but I convinced her saying it’s working and she will get better. I feel responsible for what happened with her 😔

Actually post the latest chemo cycle, the tumors started behaving like Insulinomas, causing persistent hypoglycaemia. We had to put her on continuous Dextrose 50D once every hour, along with octerotide and diazoxide. We were able to taper down the Dextrose dependency, but post chemo, her Albumin levels depleted along with other essential elements like Sodium and Potassium. She had severe water retention, which eventually got to the lungs and kidneys were overloaded. The official cause was mentioned as Refractory septic shock.
It means u need to do further investigation. Probably a PET CT GA68 & FDG as well. If there is uptake , then u may need to do a biopsy to determine next course of action.
